title: A Material-Sensitive Geometry-Dependent Strength Conversion Model for Fly Ash-Based Geopolymer Concretes with Structural Validation
content: Direct comparison of compressive strength (fc) results obtained from different specimen geometries remains a major challenge in geopolymer concrete research because it limits data consistency and the reliability of engineering assessments. Owing to the lack of strength conversion models specifically developed for geopolymer concretes, fixed conversion factors established for Ordinary Portland Cement concretes are commonly adopted. However, the mechanical behavior of geopolymer concrete is strongly influenced by matrix chemistry, activator characteristics, and curing conditions, making the use of a single fixed conversion factor questionable. In this study, the geometry-dependent fc conversion behavior of fly ash (FA)-based geopolymer concrete was investigated using a database comprising 1,247 observations from four specimen geometries. The governing parameters were identified through Pearson and Spearman correlation analyses, Mutual Information, Random Forest, and SHAP-based explainable artificial intelligence. The SiO₂/Al₂O₃ ratio and alkaline liquid-to-binder ratio were identified as the dominant parameters. Based on these findings, a geometry-dependent semi-empirical conversion model incorporating specimen volume, geopolymer matrix chemistry, and reaction efficiency was developed. The proposed model achieved higher predictive accuracy than conventional fixed conversion-factor approaches across all specimen geometries. Validation using splitting tensile strength predictions confirmed improved estimation of derived mechanical properties. Structural validation of reinforced concrete columns further demonstrated that the selected conversion approach directly affects predicted load-carrying capacity, with differences reaching approximately 18% for 150×150×150 mm cube specimens at higher strength levels. The proposed model provides a practical framework for harmonizing fc data and improving the reliability of structural analysis and design of FA-based geopolymer concrete members.
